project.objective: Who were the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota?

questions.question: Who were the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota?
questions.rationale: The objective is a single parentage fact for the subject, and no question covers it yet. The tree gives Reuben no parent links; it records a 1910 residence in Belle Prairie Township, Beadle County, South Dakota, which is context for where the family lived. Two parents are one fact, so the question asks for both together.

search_stop.justification: Overturn risk: high. Wrap-up at the researcher's request; not a declaration of reasonable exhaustiveness. Every active-plan item is closed (pli_001 to pli_008 completed; pli_009 and pli_010 user-declined). Accessible findings: the 1910 census (src_001, log_002/log_005) lists Rueben S as son of John W and Charlotte Spriggs, and the 1898 Lutheran baptism (src_003, log_023) is recorded as naming both parents; log_023 marked that baptism needs-review (index birth date 24 Nov 1898 against 6 Nov, place Carrington SD) and not adopted, so its parentage weight is for the proof-conclusion agent to assess. Unsearched and unreached: the Benson County birth register for 1898 held by the Clerk of District Court, Minnewaukan (decisive, physical, never requested); the NUMIDENT original application image (log_007 read the derivative index only); the Benson marriage record for John W Spriggs and Charlotte, 1883-1898 (pli_004 closed without a Benson hit; log_021 does not cover it); the 1900 and 1915 Maddock enumeration-district browses; and the Benson District Court declarations of intention (user-declined). The state birth register cannot be the gap: statewide birth registration began in 1907 per the North Dakota Vital Records page, read this session, so no state certificate existed for 1898. The researcher's view that the physical items are low-yield is recorded; the county birth register is the record that could name parents directly, so it remains the main overturn risk.

items.rationale: Reuben was born 6 Nov 1898 in Maddock, so the 1900 federal census for Benson County (name-searchable, about 92% indexed per loc_001) should show him, aged about one, in his parents' household. It is the first record that could name both parents together. Search the Spriggs household and the neighbouring households on the same enumeration page (FAN) for the parents' names, ages and birthplaces. Try variant spellings of the surname.

items.jurisdiction: Belle Prairie Township, Beadle County, South Dakota
items.rationale: The tree records Reuben in Belle Prairie Township, Beadle County, South Dakota in 1910 (a Residence fact with no source attached). The 1910 federal census, name-searchable in the national collection, tests whether that household lists his parents and their birthplaces. loc_001 does not cover Beadle County, so no county-level South Dakota item is planned here; that needs a locality survey first.

The 1915 North Dakota state census for Benson County is name-searchable but only about 51-55% indexed per loc_001. Where the Spriggs household is not found by name, browse the Maddock enumeration district. It shows whether the parents are still in Benson County and lists the children with their ages, which fixes Reuben's place among the siblings.

Dedicated parents' marriage item. loc_001 places Benson County marriage records from the late 1800s at the Clerk of District Court in Minnewaukan, and the county marriages collection is name-searchable. A marriage before 1898 would confirm the couple as a unit, give the mother's maiden name if this was her first marriage, and by its date corroborate a father named only indirectly. It does not by itself show Reuben is their child. Search for a Spriggs groom and for each marriage record of a candidate mother, not only the first one found.

loc_001 gives county birth records from the late 1890s, held by the Clerk of District Court in Minnewaukan, and the 1898 Maddock birth falls inside that window. A birth register entry may name both parents. The wiki's state birth-registration dates conflict (1907 and 1923), so do not assume a state certificate exists; the county register is the first check. Ask the clerk whether the register is held for 1898.

The national Social Security Numerical Identification file is name-searchable. An SSN application filed by Reuben (born 1898) may list his father's and mother's full names, so the record could name both parents without any local index. Whose lifespan sets the window: the subject's own application, which an adult would have made after 1936.

The tree records an obituary for Reuben dated 29 May 1998 (no text attached). A name-searchable national obituary collection covers 1980-2015. An obituary often names parents and their home towns, which would test the Maddock birth and the Benson County candidates. Treat it as a lead to verify against the original paper.

FAN item. The North Dakota cemetery records collection is name-searchable and covers the county. A burial of a Spriggs parent, or of a relative who names the household, would give parents' death dates and their relationships. The window runs from the birth year to about 1960, because a father born about 1860-1880 could die anywhere in that span. Also check the county tombstone sites listed in loc_001.

If the father was an immigrant, the Benson District Court declarations of intention (1884-1954) name his origin. loc_001 says these are microfilm, with originals at the State Historical Society of North Dakota, so this item is browse-only, not a name search. Use it to confirm a Spriggs or other candidate father's arrival and origin before the marriage and birth records are read.
items.skip_reason: Researcher is wrapping up q_001; the Benson District Court declarations search was not run. Parentage is reported as answered by the baptism record and the 1910 census.

Household as indexed: John W Spriggs (b. 1872 Iowa, married, head per the Couple edge), Charlotte Spriggs (b. 1877 Norway, married), Rueben S (b. 1899 ND, single, age 12 per cross-check), Lillian F (b. 1900 Iowa), Leonard W (b. 1907 SD). Selvin Christianson (b. 1884 Iowa, single) also listed. Parent-child edges link Rueben to John W and Charlotte. Relationship to head is recorded by this 1910 schedule. Not yet extracted; no sources or assertions written.

Broadened to ND state, 1900 census. 9 rows. Outside the planned jurisdiction: Benson County returned none. One household in Grand Forks, Grand Forks County ND: Ruben Spriggs (b. Dec 1865, Minnesota, married 1893), wife Florence L (b. May 1872, Pennsylvania), and children Florence L (b. May 1895 ND), Cora H (b. Aug 1896 ND), Leroy J (b. Sep 1898 ND). Cross-check vs subject (Reuben Spencer, b. 6 Nov 1898 Maddock): the name differs by one letter, the place is a different county, and the child Leroy is two months older, so a same-mother sibling is not possible; the household cannot be confirmed or excluded as the subject's parents from this index alone. needs-review. Attachment flags show attachedToOther on the household. Remaining rows are the same Ohio/WV/DC/directory rows as earlier. Ranker floor 0.01, subject not resolvable. Next: examine the Grand Forks household on its original page and anchor on the subject's birth record or a parent name.

Read of top NUMIDENT match 6KWW-PLZX (Reuben S Spriggs). Index shows birth 6 Nov 1898 (matches subject exactly), death 21 May 1998, SS claim 6 Apr 1966, residence Dana Point, California. The index entry names NO parents, so it does not yet answer the parentage question. Parents' names may appear on the original application image, which this read did not reach. Derivative index only, original not examined.

log.notes: Collection mismatch: 9,326 matches, but the top 50 ranked are census (1900, 1910, 1915, 1920, 1925, 1930, 1940, 1950), cemetery, pension, WWI draft and NUMIDENT records. None is a marriage record, and none shows a marriage in Benson County 1883-1898. The marriage-place filter did not restrict the pool to marriages. The 1893 marriage dates on two Grand Forks census-index entries (Ruben Spriggs, Florence L Spriggs) are not Benson County and do not match the plan's place. Attached-to-other hits are not evidence for John W Spriggs. Next: a marriage-typed search.

Obituary check for Reuben Spencer Spriggs (d. 21 May 1998, Dana Point CA). Full-text corpus, all collections; year filter 1998 applied. Zero results. Nil retained no sidecar. Unfiltered retry logged next.

Unfiltered retry of the 1998-filtered nil. 3708 hits, 5 examined. Top hits are 1833-1889 deeds and wills (Georgia, West Virginia, Ohio) and an 1902 Ohio probate. None is an obituary and none names a Reuben Spriggs in a North Dakota or California context. Only 5 of 3708 were read, so this is not an exhaustive check.

Only hit: Harrisburg, Pennsylvania newspaper 1973 (Pennsylvania Biographies collection). Dana Point appears as a place name in an unrelated item; Spriggs is a different person (Sandra Spriggs). Not the subject's obituary.

214 hits, 5 examined. Relevant but not the subject: a 1995 North Dakota obituary naming Leo E. Spriggs and Geneva Spriggs of Maddock/Benson County (family of Fred E Spriggs household); a 1976-79 ND obituary naming Geneva Spriggs and Leo Spriggs. Neither names Reuben. The Maddock family is in the corpus, and a 1998 obituary for Reuben would not carry the Maddock link in its text unless it named family.

495 hits, 5 examined. Riverside and California matches are in a 1975 Harrisburg PA newspaper, a 1908 PA newspaper, a Texas society record and a 1964 Georgia sports page. No Reuben Spriggs obituary among the top 5.

Name-field variant, no filters. 5.3 million hits, which is the OR default on a common name field. Top 5 are Georgia, Ohio and West Virginia deeds and wills, none the subject. Name-field retry is the nil-recovery variant for the Keywords searches.

Marriage-typed search returned 2 hits, both from the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America records collection (John Spriggs as Father-in-law; Spriggs as Father). Neither is a marriage record of a Spriggs groom in North Dakota 1883-1898, and the ranker scored neither above 0.01 against the subject (real negative). Not a marriage of John W Spriggs to Charlotte. The jurisdiction hints point to South Dakota, Minnesota and Beadle County, SD residences, not to Benson County marriages. The Benson County marriage collection did not surface under this query, so the plan item stays in_progress.

query.birthPlace: Maddock, Benson, North Dakota, United States

log.notes: Birth search for Reuben Spencer Spriggs, b. 1893-1903, birthPlace Maddock, Benson, ND. 554 total; 50 ranked. No birth-register or county-register record for Maddock/Benson County among them. Top ranked hits are census, pension, muster and SSA NUMIDENT entries. Closest in-window hits: Reuben S Spriggs NUMIDENT (birth 6 Nov 1898, no birthplace, not attached to subject); Reuben Spencer Spriggs obituary index (birth about 1899, Maddock, Benson, ND, attached to subject, d. 1998 Riverside CA). Neither is a birth record. Negative for the county register target in this index.

North Dakota state-wide check: surname Spriggs, given Reuben, recordSubdivision North Dakota, birth year 1898 exact. One hit, not a delayed birth certificate: Ruben Spencer Spriggs, Evangelical Lutheran Church baptism dated 6 Nov 1898, place indexed Carrington, South Dakota (Carrington is in Foster County, ND; the state is mis-indexed). Index birthDate 24 Nov 1898 conflicts with the tree's 6 Nov 1898. Place is Carrington, not Maddock. Score 0.97, unattached. Cross-check: name spelled Ruben, not Reuben; birth year agrees; place and index birth date do not. Status: needs-review, possible same person; not adopted. No North Dakota delayed-certificate collection surfaced in this search.

Catalog nil: no catalog entry for a Benson County birth register under this place and keyword. Not evidence that no register exists or was kept for 1898; the catalog may hold it under another title. Next: retry under a different keyword or a parent place.

Father-anchored ND search. 3 hits, none a John W Spriggs in North Dakota. Hits: John H Spriggs (b. Dec 1868, DC, single, not ND); Leroy J Spriggs (b. Sep 1898 ND, Grand Forks, household of Ruben Spriggs, already seen in log_006); a directory entry for Mrs Sprigg. No ND John W found.

Father-anchored national search, 360 hits, first 20 read. No John W Spriggs with an Iowa birth or a North Dakota or South Dakota residence in the 1900 census among the 20. Birth-year and birthplace fit seen: John W Spriggs b. Apr 1872 Maryland (Montgomery Co MD, Black, married 1894) and John W Spriggs b. May 1877 Ohio (Pike Co OH, married). Not Iowa-born; not confirmed as the subject's father. Remaining 340 unread; narrowing by Iowa birthplace next.

Narrowed national search (Iowa birth, 1869-1875). 2 hits, one a real candidate needing review: J Spriggs, b. Nov 1869 Iowa, Ross Township, Cherokee County, Kansas, 1900, married 1893, head of household. Not ND or SD. Initial J only, not John W; birth year about 2-3 years earlier than the expected 1872; Kansas residence. Cross-check: an 1869 birth against ~1872 is a gap over two years, so this is needs-review and not adopted as the father. Second hit is the directory entry Mrs Sprigg. Settling anchors would be a wife or child name matching Reuben's mother, or an ND or SD 1900 household. The collection named is the 1900 census.

proof_summaries.exhaustive_search_summary: Searched (research log): the 1910 US census household (src_001), the SSA NUMIDENT derivative index (src_002), and the 1898 Evangelical Lutheran Church baptism index entry (src_003); index searches for Benson County births and marriages returned no Benson record. Wrap-up at the researcher's request; not a declaration of reasonable exhaustiveness. Not searched: the Benson County birth register for 1898 (Clerk of District Court, Minnewaukan), which could name the parents directly; the NUMIDENT original application image; a Benson County marriage record for John W Spriggs and Charlotte, 1883-1898; the 1900 and 1915 Maddock census browses; Benson probate, land, tax and newspaper records; Benson District Court declarations of intention (user-declined); Esmond/Flora church registers (user-declined). These would corroborate or directly confirm the parentage already indicated; none is known to contradict it. State birth registration began in 1907, so no state certificate exists for 1898.
proof_summaries.narrative_markdown: ## Conclusion The evidence indicates that Reuben Spencer Spriggs (born 6 November 1898, reported as Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota; died 21 May 1998) was the son of **John W Spriggs** and **Charlotte Spriggs**. The finding is probable, not proved: two independent derivative sources agree, but no original birth record has been examined. ## Evidence **1898 Lutheran baptism (src_003).** The index entry records "Ruben Spencer Spriggs, child of J W Spriggs, child of Charlotte Spriggs," christening 6 Nov 1898. Information came from the presenting parent and the officiant (primary, direct, stated). The full name, with the middle name Spencer, matches the subject, and the christening date equals the subject's known birth date. Source: "United States, Evangelical Lutheran Church in America records, ca. 1800-1900," database with images, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:QK1L-SKL7 : 31 July 2026), 06 Nov 1898; citing Carrington, South Dakota, United States, Baptism; from Ancestry. www.ancestry.com, Multiple archives, United States; FHL microfilm 100,881,426. The source is a derivative index of a church register. **1910 census (src_001).** Rueben S Spriggs, age 11, born North Dakota, appears as son of the head John W Spriggs (38, born Iowa) in a household with wife Charlotte Spriggs (33, born Norway), Lillian F (10) and Leonard W (3), Prairie Belle, Beadle County, South Dakota. Informants are unidentified household members (indeterminate quality; stated). The relationship column names the child's relation to the head, so it directly supports only the father; Charlotte's motherhood is inferred from her position as the head's wife, with an age (about 22 at the 1898 birth) that fits. Source: "United States, Census, 1910", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MPXD-MZ4 : Wed Aug 13 17:11:01 UTC 2025), Entry for John W Spriggs and Charlotte Spriggs, 1910. Derivative. **SSA NUMIDENT (src_002).** Reuben S Spriggs, born 6 Nov 1898, died 21 May 1998, Dana Point, California. It names no parents but ties the subject's birth date to the christening date. Source: "United States, Social Security Numerical Identification Files (NUMIDENT), 1936-2007", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6KWW-PLZX : Tue Jul 07 02:13:34 UTC 2026), Entry for Reuben S Spriggs. Derivative; birth date is secondary information. ## Discrepancies in the baptism entry 1. **Birth date.** The index gives birth 24 Nov 1898 but christening 6 Nov 1898. A birth cannot follow its christening, so the 24 Nov reading is internally unreliable (likely a transposition or indexing error), whereas the 6 Nov date matches the NUMIDENT birth date exactly. The year is not in dispute. 2. **Place.** The entry is indexed at Carrington, South Dakota. Carrington is in Foster County, North Dakota, so the state is probably mis-indexed. In any case the place is that of the christening, not the birth, so it does not contradict a Maddock birth, and the family's mobility (children born in North Dakota, Iowa and South Dakota between 1898 and 1907) makes a nearby church plausible. Neither discrepancy touches the parents' names, which the two independent sources give consistently, and neither is registered as a conflict. A second family naming a child Ruben Spencer Spriggs to parents J W and Charlotte in 1898 is not indicated by any record in hand. ## Correlation and tier Two independent derivative sources agree on the father; the baptism and the census household together point to Charlotte as mother. Identity of J W with John W rests on initials plus the shared mother's name and child. The 1910 census alone could not distinguish a stepmother, but the baptism names Charlotte as mother 12 years earlier. Against a higher tier: both sources are derivative indexes, the baptism carries internal errors, Charlotte's identity link is moderate (score 0.73), and the county birth register has not been examined. Hence probable. This conclusion could be overturned only by the unsearched records named in the exhaustive-search summary; none is known to disagree. Tree: ParentChild John W Spriggs (I1) to Reuben (L64C-QQX) already existed; Charlotte Spriggs (I2) to Reuben was added from these sources.

quirks: Benson County was organized 9 March 1883 from DeSmet and Ramsey Counties, with Minnewaukan as county seat (North Dakota Genealogy wiki, Boundary Changes). Records for 1880-1883 may sit under the predecessor counties; search DeSmet and Ramsey for anything before March 1883.

Maddock is a city within Benson County (place search: Maddock, Benson, North Dakota, from 1897). Search the county series for Maddock births; the 1898 birth falls within the county's own record period.

The Benson County wiki chart gives county birth records from the late 1890s and county death records from 1895; the Benson page states state Department of Vital Records began births and deaths in 1923. The North Dakota Vital Records page instead gives statewide birth and death registration from 1907, generally complied with by 1924. These dates conflict; verify with the county Clerk of District Court and the state before relying on either.
The Benson County page places county court, land and probate records from 1883 and county census from 1836 in its chart; the chart is a guide only and says dates often conflict.
Catalog hit koha:655787 is a partial index to the 1885 census of northern Dakota Territory covering Benson County (FamilySearch Library; also on microfilm 1425174).
Catalog hit koha:1009663 (Declarations of intention, 1884-1954) is microfilm of originals now at the State Historical Society of North Dakota in Bismarck; a general index is on film 2196714.

Church records for Esmond (1830-1958, 36% name-indexed, Norwegian and English) and Flora (1820-1997, 34% name-indexed, Norwegian and English) are digitized in FamilySearch; the survey did not confirm which parish served Maddock, so do not assume these registers cover Maddock families.
Online indexes are incomplete. A negative result is not absence: search variant spellings and check microfilm and physical holdings.
Fort Totten lies in Benson County; the Fort Totten history catalog entry (koha:515092) includes 1870 and 1880 census lists for Fort Totten and Devils Lake Mission.

localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Benson County, North Dakota (incl. Maddock) (1880-1920)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 9 March 1883 from DeSmet and Ramsey Counties (Benson County, North Dakota Genealogy wiki)
- **County seat / administrative center:** Minnewaukan
- **Parent jurisdiction:** North Dakota (Dakota Territory before statehood; the survey did not return a territorial-era series for the county beyond the 1885 partial census index)
- **Population during period:** The survey returned state population only (North Dakota, 1880: 36,900; 1890: 191,000; 1900: 319,100; 1910: 577,100; 1920: 646,900). No county figure was returned.
- **Economy:** not confirmed by this survey
- **Ethnic composition:** Norwegian-language church records are digitized for Esmond and Flora; the survey did not confirm the wider ethnic mix.
- **Religious denominations:** Lutheran and Dutch Reformed collections are listed by the wiki; Esmond and Flora church records are digitized.
- **Key historical events:** Fort Totten, established 1867, became an industrial school in 1890 (catalog koha:515092).
- **Coverage of this survey:** 14 digitized volumes match the place (complete); all 14 are listed in the survey, with no paging gap. Catalog: 13 hits, 3 listed.

## Boundary changes
- Benson County was created 9 March 1883 from DeSmet and Ramsey Counties, Dakota Territory (Benson County wiki, Boundary Changes). Records for the period before March 1883 are under the predecessor counties.
- The Newberry Library Atlas of Historical County Boundaries and its county chronology list every boundary change; the wiki links these, but the survey did not read them.
- Maddock is a city in Benson County from 1897 per the place record.

## Research tips
- **Search order:** Start with the 1900 federal census volume (92% name-indexed) and the 1915 state census for Benson County, both free on FamilySearch, to fix household members and birth years. Next, the Benson County Clerk of District Court in Minnewaukan for county birth, marriage and probate records, which the wiki says begin in the late 1890s, late 1800s and 1883. Then the offline and browse-only volumes.
- The county's birth register may begin in the late 1890s (Benson County wiki); the 1898 Maddock birth falls inside that window. Ask the clerk whether it is held. The state dates conflict (see quirks), so do not assume a state certificate exists for 1898.
- Maddock is in the county: search the county series for Maddock families and do not limit the search to Maddock's own records.
- Church records: Esmond (1830-1958) and Flora (1820-1997) registers are digitized, in English and Norwegian. The survey did not confirm which parish served Maddock; treat them as candidates only after confirming the parish.
- Immigration and naturalization: the District Court declarations of intention (1884-1954) are on microfilm; originals are at the State Historical Society of North Dakota in Bismarck (catalog koha:1009663).
- The 1885 census index for Benson County is partial (catalog koha:655787).
- Neighbouring counties (Benson County wiki): Eddy, Nelson, Pierce, Ramsey, Towner, Wells. Search these for family members who moved across county lines.
- Online indexes are incomplete; a negative search is not proof of absence. Check spelling variants of the surname and the other records named above.
- Naming customs: the survey did not return a Benson-specific naming page; the general United States Naming Customs page lists only online resources.
